If an expected MCP tool is not visible:

1. Do not switch to `gh` or any other route.
2. Re-check discovery — the tool may be namespaced, paginated, or reachable
   through a different method.
3. If it is genuinely absent, or the server is down or unauthenticated: stop
   and report the blocker to the owner with what was tried.

# Issue #27 — Fix summary

Fixes 8 defects in 4 files of the header-only TiffCraft library; one focused PR, no build-system changes.

## Files changed

| File | Defect(s) | Change |
|------|-----------|--------|
| `include/tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp` | D1, D2(a), D2(c), D3 | `inline` on `version()`, `readAt()`, `writeAt()`, both `load()` overloads; `#include <set>`; visited-set in `TiffImage::read(istream&)` throws `std::runtime_error` on cyclic IFD offsets; `readAt` throws after short reads (`!stream` or `gcount() != size`); ASCII `valueSize == 0` throws `std::runtime_error`; additionally guarded `std::memcpy` with `valueSize > 0` (found via UBSan probe: `memcpy(nullptr, &value, 0)` is UB) |
| `include/tiffcraft/TiffStdOut.hpp` | D1, D8 | six `operator<<` overloads moved into `namespace TiffCraft` and marked `inline`; removed now-redundant `using namespace TiffCraft;` inside the Entry operator; `Type::BYTE` printed via `static_cast<int>` |
| `include/tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp` | D2(b), D4, D5 | `makeIntVec` throws `std::runtime_error` on zero rational denominator (covers RATIONAL and SRATIONAL via `is_rational_v`); `takeImage()` drops `const`; `TiffExporterAny::operator()` resets `exported_ = false` per IFD invocation |
| `examples/tiff_image.cpp` | D6 | type-agnostic `readDimension` lambda for `ImageWidth`/`ImageLength` (SHORT/LONG, clear error otherwise) |
| `README.md` | D7 | dropped undeclared `loadParams` argument; `iffExporter` → `tiffExporter` |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | docs | `### Fixed` subsection added under `## [0.2.0-Unreleased]` listing all 8 defect classes (notes the `operator<<` namespace move for downstream users) |

Scope: no CMake/build/packaging changes; no new test files; no sanitizer config; fixtures untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Status | Evidence |
|----|--------|----------|
| AC1 — existing tests pass | PASS | `ctest --preset gcc-linux-release --output-on-failure` → 2/2 tests passed (`tiffImageTest`, `tiffExporterTest`) |
| AC2 — two-TU link test | PASS | two TUs each including `TiffStdOut.hpp` compile and link cleanly (ad hoc `g++ -std=c++20 -I include`) |
| AC3 — example runs on LONG-ImageWidth fixtures | PASS | `tiff_image_example` on `pc260001.tif` (640x480), `dscf0013.tif` (both IFDs: 640x480, 160x120), `smallliz.tif` (160x160) — no exceptions |
| AC4 — malformed TIFF probes throw, no crash/hang | PASS | ASan/UBSan probes with `timeout 10`: ASCII count==0 → `runtime_error: ASCII entry must contain at least one byte`; rational denom==0 → `runtime_error: Rational value with zero denominator in TIFF entry`; cyclic IFD → `runtime_error: Cyclic IFD offset detected in TIFF file`; truncated strip → `runtime_error: Failed to read the requested number of bytes from the stream`. No sanitizer reports, no hangs |
| AC5 — `takeImage()` leaves exporter buffer empty | PASS | probe on `jim___ah.tif`: before `dataSize=539832`, after `takeImage()` `dataSize=0` |
| AC6 — README example compiles | PASS | corrected snippet compiles with `g++ -std=c++20 -I include -c`; matches `examples/tiff_exporter.cpp` (compiled by the build) |

Multi-IFD probe (synthetic 2-IFD 8-bit grayscale TIFF): `TiffExporterAny` exports both IFDs, last-wins → final buffer holds IFD 2 pixels (`200 210 220 230`), confirming the D5 reset. `Type::BYTE` probe: value `0x41` now prints as `65`.

## Side effects and follow-ups

- **Behavior change (intended):** malformed input now throws `std::runtime_error` instead of UB/hang/silent zeros.
- **Behavior change (observable):** the six `operator<<` overloads moved from the global namespace into `namespace TiffCraft`; found via ADL. Any downstream qualified `::operator<<` references break; unqualified usage is unaffected. Noted in CHANGELOG.
- **Behavior change (intended):** `takeImage()` no longer const; `image_` is left moved-from (empty). Only signature change in the PR.
- **Behavior change (intended):** `TiffExporterAny` multi-IFD semantics: "first IFD wins / stale skip" → "each IFD resets `exported_`; last successfully exported IFD wins". A failing IFD still throws `FormatNotSupportedError`.
- **Behavior change (user-visible):** `Type::BYTE` entries print as integers.
- **Extra in-scope hardening:** `std::memcpy` in `Entry::read` is now skipped when `valueSize == 0` (fixes `memcpy(nullptr, ..., 0)` UB flagged by UBSan on the ASCII count==0 probe). Not a new defect; required for the D2(a)/AC4 probe to be sanitizer-clean.
- Follow-ups (not done, out of scope): no registered regression tests for malformed input (scope guardrail); no fuzzing infrastructure.

## Docs

README quick-start fixed (D7); CHANGELOG `### Fixed` added under `[0.2.0-Unreleased]`; header doc comments unchanged (the `TiffExporter.hpp` embedded example was already correct).

Resolves #27

{"number":28,"title":"#27: Fix critical bugs: ODR violations, crashers on malformed input, and broken example","body":"# Issue #27 — Fix summary

Fixes 8 defects in 4 files of the header-only TiffCraft library; one focused PR, no build-system changes.

## Files changed

| File | Defect(s) | Change |
|------|-----------|--------|
| include/tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp | D1, D2(a), D2(c), D3 | `inline` on `version()`, `readAt()`, `writeAt()`, both `load()` overloads; visited-set in `TiffImage::read(istream&)` throws `std::runtime_error` on cyclic IFD offsets; `readAt` throws after short reads; ASCII `valueSize == 0` throws `std::runtime_error`; guarded `std::memcpy` with `valueSize > 0` (UBSan) |
| include/tiffcraft/TiffStdOut.hpp | D1, D8 | six `operator<<` overloads moved into `namespace TiffCraft` and marked `inline`; `Type::BYTE` printed via `static_cast<int>` |
| include/tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp | D2(b), D4, D5 | `makeIntVec` throws `std::runtime_error` on zero rational denominator; `takeImage()` drops `const`; `TiffExporterAny::operator()` resets `exported_ = false` per IFD invocation |
| examples/tiff_image.cpp | D6 | type-agnostic `readDimension` lambda for `ImageWidth`/`ImageLength` (SHORT/LONG) |
| README.md | D7 | dropped undeclared `loadParams` argument; `iffExporter` → `tiffExporter` |
| CHANGELOG.md | docs | `### Fixed` subsection under `## [0.2.0-Unreleased]` |

Scope: no CMake/build/packaging changes; no new test files; no sanitizer config; fixtures untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Status | Evidence |
|----|--------|----------|
| AC1 — existing tests pass | PASS | `ctest --preset gcc-linux-release --output-on-failure` → 2/2 tests passed |
| AC2 — two-TU link test | PASS | two TUs each including TiffStdOut.hpp compile and link cleanly |
| AC3 — example runs on LONG-ImageWidth fixtures | PASS | tiff_image_example on pc260001.tif (640x480), dscf0013.tif (both IFDs), smallliz.tif (160x160) — no exceptions |
| AC4 — malformed TIFF probes throw, no crash/hang | PASS | ASan/UBSan probes with timeout: ASCII count==0 → `runtime_error: ASCII entry must contain at least one byte`; rational denom==0 → `runtime_error: Rational value with zero denominator in TIFF entry`; cyclic IFD → `runtime_error: Cyclic IFD offset detected in TIFF file`; truncated strip → `runtime_error: Failed to read the requested number of bytes from the stream` |
| AC5 — takeImage() leaves exporter buffer empty | PASS | probe on jim___ah.tif: before dataSize=539832, after takeImage() dataSize=0 |
| AC6 — README example compiles | PASS | corrected snippet compiles with `g++ -std=c++20 -I include -c` |

Multi-IFD probe (synthetic 2-IFD 8-bit grayscale TIFF): TiffExporterAny exports both IFDs, last-wins → final buffer holds IFD 2 pixels (200 210 220 230). Type::BYTE probe: value 0x41 now prints as 65.

## Side effects and follow-ups

- Behavior change (intended): malformed input throws std::runtime_error instead of UB/hang/silent zeros.
- Behavior change (observable): the six operator<< overloads moved from global namespace into namespace TiffCraft; found via ADL. Downstream qualified ::operator<< references break; unqualified usage unaffected. Noted in CHANGELOG.
- Behavior change (intended): takeImage() no longer const; image_ is left moved-from (empty).
- Behavior change (intended): TiffExporterAny multi-IFD semantics: first IFD wins → each IFD resets exported_; last successfully exported IFD wins. A failing IFD still throws FormatNotSupportedError.
- Behavior change (user-visible): Type::BYTE entries print as integers.
- Extra in-scope hardening: std::memcpy in Entry::read skipped when valueSize == 0 (memcpy(nullptr, ..., 0) UB flagged by UBSan on the ASCII count==0 probe).
- Follow-ups (out of scope): no registered regression tests for malformed input; no fuzzing infrastructure.

## Docs

README quick-start fixed (D7); CHANGELOG ### Fixed added under [0.2.0-Unreleased]; header doc comments unchanged.

Resolves #27

2. Minor: PR body side-effect wording contradictory ("first IFD wins" vs "last successfully exported IFD wins"); clarify multi-IFD semantics in PR body/CHANGELOG.

Now — Standing order 2: review comments on the PR are requests for this PR's code only, implement it. The issue scope said "No CMake changes... no new registered tests (ad hoc verification only)" — but the owner (who wrote the issue AND the PR comment/review) explicitly requests tests. The review is explicit owner order: "Please add tests." That overrides the issue scope note. Ordered scope ships. Adding tests requires touching tests/ and CMakeLists.txt (test registration). The issue said no CMake changes, but the owner's PR review explicitly orders regression tests including "so AC4/AC5/AC6 are enforceable in CI" and "add targeted tests (and a two-TU link check)". Two-TU link check "enforceable in CI" implies adding a CMake target too? Hmm — "Please add targeted tests (and a two-TU link check) so AC4/AC5/AC6 are enforceable in CI."

Options: add tests to tests/tiffImageTest.cpp + tests/tiffExporterTest.cpp (registered already via ctest), and add a two-TU link check test. The two-TU link check could be a small CMake addition: e.g., a test that compiles two TUs? That's harder in CMake. Common approach: create two object files from two .cpp files and link them as a test executable. E.g., add tests/two_tu_main.cpp/tests/two_tu_other.cpp and a target. That's a CMake change — but owner ordered it. The issue scope restriction ("No CMake changes") vs direct owner order in review: an explicit owner order wins ("Out-of-scope work... happen only on an explicit owner order — a direct directive to act, in any wording that unambiguously orders it"). "Please add targeted tests (and a two-TU link check) so AC4/AC5/AC6 are enforceable in CI" is an unambiguous order. So CMake additions for tests are authorized.

Also fix minor: clarify multi-IFD semantics wording in PR body and CHANGELOG. CHANGELOG currently says "TiffExporterAny now resets its multi-IFD state per IFD, so images with multiple IFDs export correctly instead of silently skipping later IFDs." — not contradictory. The PR body says: "Multi-IFD probe ... last-wins" and "first IFD wins → each IFD resets exported_; last successfully exported IFD wins" — hmm, that's not contradictory either... the review says "PR body side-effect note is internally contradictory ('first IFD wins' vs 'last successfully exported IFD wins')". I should reword the side-effect bullet to clearly state last-wins semantics. And CHANGELOG: could add "last-wins" wording. Update both + PR body via update_pull_request.

Plan:
1. Add tests to tests/tiffImageTest.cpp and/or new test files? Follow repo conventions: existing tests in tiffImageTest.cpp / tiffExporterTest.cpp with doctest. Adding to those files keeps CMake unchanged except maybe two-TU check. For the two-TU link check enforceable in CI: create tests/two_tu_link_a.cpp and tests/two_tu_link_b.cpp, and a CMake target (add_executable) plus add_test. That's the cleanest. But wait — the two-TU check: if both TUs include TiffStdOut.hpp and both define main? No — one TU defines main (the doctest main?) Better: two TUs with no main, linked... CMake requires executables to have a main. Create two_tu_link_test.cpp? Design: file A defines function with operator<< usage, file B defines another function + main? Or: tu_a.cpp has no main, tu_b.cpp has main and calls into A; both include TiffStdOut.hpp and use operator<< for TiffCraft types. Target two_tu_test (or similar), add_test it. Names: tests/twoTuLinkTestA.cpp? Follow naming: existing files tiffImageTest.cpp, tiffExporterTest.cpp. I'll add tests/two_tu_link_test_a.cpp, two_tu_link_test_b.cpp? Hmm, maybe single-purpose: `tests/twoTULinkTest.cpp` with a `#include` of the second TU? No — the whole point is two separate TUs. So two files + CMake target + add_test + link against TiffCraft INTERFACE.

Wait — do the tests really need CMake changes? The two-TU target must be added to tests/CMakeLists.txt. That's the natural way to make it CI-enforceable. Proceed.

Tests to add:
tiffImageTest.cpp (or a new file?):
- ASCII entry count==0 → load() throws (CHECK_THROWS / doctest: CHECK_THROWS_AS(..., std::runtime_error))
- RATIONAL denominator==0 → via TiffExporter::getIntVec throws — but tiffImageTest.cpp includes TiffImage.hpp and TiffStdOut.hpp, not TiffExporter.hpp. Add getIntVec probe in tiffExporterTest.cpp? makeIntVec is protected? It's public static? Check: `static std::vector<int> makeIntVec` at line 167 — need to see if public. Line 144 class TiffExporter — class (not struct), default private? Line 144 `class TiffExporter` and statics at 167... then `public:` somewhere? Let me check. I'll read the file around those lines to determine access. Also tests use TiffExporterGray etc. from the test file.
- Cyclic IFD → load/read throws.
- Truncated strip → load() throws.
- LONG ImageWidth example handling: that's example code, hard to test without refactoring the example. AC3 is "example runs on fixtures" — can't easily test example in ctest. But could add a test that loads pc260001.tif with LONG ImageWidth and reads via values<uint32_t> — that tests the pattern but not the example. The review asks: "add targeted tests (and a two-TU link check) so AC4/AC5/AC6 are enforceable in CI. AC4/AC5 are tests; AC6 is README compile — enforceable via a "readme snippet compile" check? That'd be heavy. Reasonable interpretation: tests for the fixed behaviors (AC4 crash paths, AC5 takeImage, multi-IFD, BYTE printing, ODR two-TU link, LONG dimension read pattern). AC6 (README compiles) — maybe a CMake check compiling a README-derived snippet? That might be overkill; I could add a test that compiles? Can't compile at test time easily... Actually you CAN: add a test that runs a compiled snippet. The README snippet is not in the build. Simplest faithful implementation: create tests/readmeUsageExample.cpp containing the exact README quick-start snippet (guarded, returns 0), add it as an executable (two_tu style). Then CI compiling it enforces AC6. Hmm, but duplicating the README snippet in a test file creates drift risk. The review explicitly says "so AC4/AC5/AC6 are enforceable in CI."

Let me design minimal additions without over-engineering:
New test files:
1. `tests/twoTULinkTestA.cpp` + `tests/twoTULinkTestB.cpp` — wait, maybe reuse pattern: a non-doctest plain executable `twoTuLinkTest` (one TU with main, one without), add_test runs it. This covers AC2/ODR.
2. README snippet check: extend that same non-doctest approach? The README snippet needs main too — can't have two mains in one target. Option: `tests/readmeUsageTest.cpp` compiled as object lib? Simpler: add README snippet compile as a CMAKE target without main? It has main. Alternative: three small targets is fine. Or a single `usageExampleTest.cpp` that IS the README snippet (main + TiffExporterAny + load + takeImage), failing at runtime? It just returns 0 — ctest passes. Use it for both AC6 and AC2? No, AC2 requires two TUs each including TiffStdOut.hpp. Keep separate.

Hmm, but "don't over-engineer" — the review is a request for tests; I should implement faithfully but minimally. Proposal:

tests/CMakeLists.txt additions:
```cmake
add_executable(twoTuLinkTest twoTuLinkTestA.cpp twoTuLinkTestB.cpp)
target_link_libraries(twoTuLinkTest PRIVATE TiffCraft)
add_test(NAME twoTuLinkTest COMMAND twoTuLinkTest)
add_executable(readmeUsageTest readmeUsageTest.cpp)
target_link_libraries(readmeUsageTest PRIVATE TiffCraft)
add_test(NAME readmeUsageTest COMMAND readmeUsageTest)
```

readmeUsageTest.cpp = exact README quick-start (argc check, TiffExporterAny, load, takeImage) + return 0; but as a test it should run — load(argv[1]) requires argv[1] fixture; pass fixture arg: add_test(NAME readmeUsageTest COMMAND readmeUsageTest ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libtiff-pics/pc260001.tif). README snippet with argc<2 returns 1 — with the arg passes. Good — this also enforces the exporter works on the LONG-ImageWidth RGB fixture at runtime.

three test targets added. Wait — should README usage test duplicate README? Ideal is compile-check of README snippet; hard in CMake without extracting. I'll note in the test file header comment: "Keep in sync with README.md quick-start." That enforces AC6 reasonably.

UNIT tests in tiffImageTest.cpp (doctest):
- TEST_CASE("malformed TIFF inputs"): 
  - ASCII entry with count 0 → TiffImage::read / load throws std::runtime_error. Need to craft TIFF bytes in-memory — the file has write_IFD_entry helper. Let me read tests/tiffImageTest.cpp to match style and reuse helpers.
  - RATIONAL denominator 0 → hmm, getIntVec needs TiffExporter.hpp. tiffImageTest.cpp doesn't include it. Put the rational test in tiffExporterTest.cpp (it includes TiffExporter.hpp) or include TiffExporter.hpp in tiffImageTest.cpp. Better: rational test in tiffExporterTest.cpp.
  - cyclic IFD → tiffImageTest.cpp.
  - truncated strip → tiffImageTest.cpp (load with callback throws runtime_error).
- takeImage test in tiffExporterTest.cpp? AC5 — TestExporter exists there (custom exporter subclass for tests). TiffExporterAny takeImage: load jim___ah.tif with TiffExporterAny, takeImage, check image().data empty. tiffExporterTest.cpp includes TiffExporter.hpp and uses libtiff-pics — good place.
- multi-IFD export test: synthetic 2-IFD grayscale TIFF built byte-by-byte — I already have multiifd_gray.tif bytes generator... but committing binary fixture? Could synthesize in-code like existing tests do. Simpler: multi-IFD via load() callback count on dscf0013.tif (2 IFDs) or text.tif — but TiffExporterAny on those throws FormatNotSupportedError (unsupported). For the D5 regression, better: build in-memory 2-IFD TIFF with the write_IFD helpers? Those helpers write single IFD presumably. Could hand-craft in the test: bytes for 2-IFD grayscale image (like my python). In C++ that's tedious but doable. Alternatively use existing 2-IFD fixtures text.tif/dscf0013.tif with a custom TestExporter counting invocations: "load() invokes callback for both IFDs" — that tests load, not TiffExporterAny::exported_ reset though. For the actual D5 fix, test with TiffExporterAny on a synthetic 2-IFD grayscale: needs the synthetic file. Where do tests store synthetic TIFFs? They synthesize streams in-memory. I can synthesize the multi-IFD gray TIFF in a std::stringstream in the test using the same byte patterns as my python script. That's the most robust, no fixture needed.

Let me read the test files to match conventions and helper availability before planning implementation. Also check whether TiffExporter class statics are public (makeIntVec/getIntVec) — used in tests.

This is a chunk of work. Delegate implementation to a general sub-agent with detailed instructions, after I read the test files myself to give precise guidance. Let me read both test files' key sections.

The owner (via PR #28 review and comment) requested regression tests. That review is an explicit order and overrides the issue's "no new tests" scope note. Let me look at the test files to plan the additions.

You are adding regression tests to the repo /home/daniel/tiffcraft on branch bugfix/issue-27 (already checked out), addressing PR #28 review feedback: "No regression tests for the new behavior... add targeted tests (and a two-TU link check) so AC4/AC5/AC6 are enforceable in CI." and the owner comment "Please add tests."

This is an authorized owner order that overrides the issue's "no new tests" scope note. Keep changes minimal, follow repo conventions (doctest, TEST_CASE, existing helper style), keep the license header style, and do NOT modify library source (include/tiffcraft/*) except none. Only add files under tests/, modify tests/CMakeLists.txt minimally, and touch CHANGELOG.md wording (see D5 wording fix below).

FIRST read these files fully: tests/tiffImageTest.cpp, tests/tiffExporterTest.cpp, tests/CMakeLists.txt, tests/netpbm.hpp (head), CHANGELOG.md (the [0.2.0-Unreleased] Fixed section), README.md (quick-start).

### Tests to add

**A. In tests/tiffImageTest.cpp** (new TEST_CASEs; the file includes <tiffcraft/TiffCraft.hpp> which re-exports TiffImage.hpp and TiffExporter.hpp, and TiffStdOut.hpp; it defines write_IFD_entry / write_IFD / writeValue helpers and DOCTEST_CONFIG_IMPLEMENT_WITH_MAIN):

1. TEST_CASE("Malformed TIFF input") with three sub-checks, synthesized in-memory (stringstreams), each expecting std::runtime_error:
   (a) ASCII entry with count == 0: hand-craft bytes directly (the write_IFD_entry helper throws on count<1, so do NOT use it). Little-endian "II", uint16 42, uint32 first IFD offset = 8; IFD at offset 8: uint16 entry count = 1; one entry: tag ASCII(0x010E ImageDescription) type=ASCII(2) count=0 value=0 (inline); uint32 next IFD offset = 0. Read via `TiffImage::read(stream)`; CHECK_THROWS_AS(..., std::runtime_error). Use `writeValue(stream, ...)` with mustSwap=false for the bytes (check writeValue's signature in TiffImage.hpp — it's used inside tests; match its usage in helpers above). Tag enum value: Tag::ImageDescription (verify name in TiffImage.hpp; if uncertain use 0x010E via static_cast<Tag>(0x010E)).
   (b) Cyclic IFD: header(II, 42, firstIFDOffset = 8); IFD at 8 with 0 entries: uint16 0, uint32 nextIFDOffset = 8 → `TiffImage::read(stream)` throws std::runtime_error.
   (c) Truncated strip: synthesize an image TIFF: StripOffsets (tag 0x0111, Type::LONG, count 1, value 100), StripByteCounts (tag 0x0117, Type::LONG, count 1, value 1000), Compression (0x0103, SHORT, 1, value 1), PhotometricInterpretation (0x0106, SHORT, 1, value 0). Build entries via the existing pattern (write each entry to a stringstream, read back with Entry::read), then write_IFD(stream, entries, false) after the 8-byte header, but do NOT write strip data — stream ends there. Then `load(stream, [](auto&&...){ }, LoadParams{})` → CHECK_THROWS_AS(..., std::runtime_error). Note load() is in TiffCraft namespace; tests use `using namespace TiffCraft`.
   Note: for (c), ensure the synthesized strip offset (100) is beyond the actual stream size so the short read trips.
   (d) Also in the same TEST_CASE: RATIONAL entry with denominator 0: XResolution (0x011A, RATIONAL, count 1, 8 bytes: numerator=300, denominator=0). Build entry via write+read round trip (valueBytes=8 > 4 → need valueOffset; simplest: hand-craft or use write_IFD_entry with valueOffset = 12+12+4+2... careful. Easier: hand-craft the whole file as in (a)/(b): header(8) + IFD: 1 entry tag 0x011A type RATIONAL(5) count 1 valueOffset = position after IFD table; compute valueOffset = 8 + 2 + 12*1 + 4 = 26; round to even 26 is even. After the next-IFD uint32 (at offset 8+2+12=22..26), place 8 bytes RATIONAL at offset 26: numerator 300 (uint32 LE) denominator 0. Then read image via TiffImage::read(stream) — Entry::read does NOT divide rationals, so this must NOT throw at read time; then call `TiffExporter::getIntVec(image.ifds()[0], Tag::XResolution)` → CHECK_THROWS_AS(..., std::runtime_error). TiffExporter is in TiffCraft namespace (makeIntVec/getIntVec are public static per include/tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp lines ~144-226 public:). Actually getIntVec is under `public:` (after protected Image image_). Confirm by reading the file; if getIntVec is not public, instead synthesize the entry and use TiffExporterGray<uint8_t> exporter load to trigger the divide — decide after reading the header.

2. TEST_CASE("LONG ImageWidth fixtures"): for pc260001.tif (path helper getTestFilePath("pc260001.tif")) and smallliz.tif — read with TiffImage::read; CHECK the ImageWidth entry type is Type::LONG; CHECK values<uint32_t>()[0] equals expected width (640 / 160) and ImageLength (480 / 160). Also verify `values<uint16_t>()` on those entries throws std::runtime_error (documents the D6 defect class) — optional; keep it.
   Note dscf0013.tif is 2 IFDs — skip it here to keep the test simple, or iterate its IFDs. Skip.

3. TEST_CASE("Type::BYTE printed as integer"): synthesize a BYTE entry with value 0x41 (65): build a stream with one BYTE entry via write_IFD_entry + Entry::read (pattern from the "IFD::Entry class" TEST_CASE), then `std::ostringstream ss; ss << entry;` CHECK(ss.str().find("65") != std::string::npos) and CHECK(ss.str().find("'A'") == std::string::npos). Requires <sstream> (already included) and TiffStdOut.hpp (included).

**B. In tests/tiffExporterTest.cpp** (includes TiffExporter.hpp, doctest main, getFilePath helper):

4. TEST_CASE("TiffExporterAny takeImage"): load getFilePath("libtiff-pics/jim___ah.tif") with std::ref(exporter) where exporter is TiffExporterAny. Before take: exporter.image().dataSize() > 0. After `auto image = exporter.takeImage();`: CHECK(exporter.image().data.size() == 0) (image() returns const Image&; data is public). CHECK(image.dataSize() > 0).

5. TEST_CASE("TiffExporterAny multi-IFD export"): synthesize a 2-IFD 8-bit grayscale TIFF in-memory — port this exact layout (verified working):
   - Header: "II", uint16 42, uint32 firstIFDOffset = 8.
   - IFD size = 2 + 9*12 + 4 = 114 bytes. Entries (tag, type, count, inline-value-or-offset):
     256 LONG 1 W(2); 257 LONG 1 H(2); 258 SHORT 1 8 (inline, low 2 bytes of the 4-byte field, value 8);
     259 SHORT 1 1 (Compression=1); 262 SHORT 1 1 (Photometric BlackIsZero); 273 LONG 1 pix_off;
     277 SHORT 1 1 (SamplesPerPixel); 278 LONG 1 H (RowsPerStrip); 279 LONG 1 4 (StripByteCounts).
     Entries need not be sorted for reading? IFD::read probably inserts into map — order-independent. Keep ascending order anyway (256,257,258,259,262,273,277,278,279).
   - ifd1 at offset 8, pix1 at offset 8+114=122 (bytes [10,20,30,40]); ifd2 at offset 126, pix2 at offset 240 (bytes [200,210,220,230]); nextIFD of ifd1 = 126; ifd2 next = 0. Wait recompute: ifd2 at 122+4 = 126; pix2 at 126+114 = 240; total file 244 bytes.
   - Build into a std::stringstream byte by byte (helper lambdas: le16(v) writes 2 bytes LE, le32(v) 4 bytes). Then `load(stream, std::ref(exporter));` with TiffExporterAny exporter. Expected: exported without exception; exporter.image().dataSize() == 4; the four pixel bytes decode to IFD2's pixels [200,210,220,230]. Access data: exporter.image().data[i] → std::byte; static_cast<unsigned char>(...) . NOTE: TiffExporterGray<uint8_t> — how does TiffExporterAny decode BlackIsZero 8-bit? It worked in my probe: pixels came out 200 210 220 230 exactly. Replicate.
   - Also CHECK that load() invoked the callback path for both IFDs is implicit; the D5 regression is: exported_ must reset per IFD; before the fix, image_ kept IFD1 pixels ([10,20,30,40]). Assert final bytes == 200,210,220,230 (i.e., IFD2 won) to pin the semantics.

**C. Two NEW plain (non-doctest) files in tests/** for the two-TU link check (ODR regression enforcement):

6. tests/twoTuLinkTestA.cpp — include license header comment (short BSD style like other test files, or a simple comment block; keep consistent):
   ```cpp
   // twoTuLinkTestA.cpp
   // Part of the two-TU ODR check: both translation units include TiffStdOut.hpp
   // and use the operator<< overloads; the link must succeed.
   #include <tiffcraft/TiffStdOut.hpp>
   #include <sstream>
   #include <string>
   std::string twoTuLinkTestA() {
     std::ostringstream os;
     os << TiffCraft::Tag::ImageWidth;
     os << TiffCraft::TiffImage::Header{};   // use the Header operator<<
     return os.str();
   }
   ```
   Wait — TiffImage::Header{} default-constructible? Check include/tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp Header struct — it had Header::read and byteOrder()... check default ctor exists. If unsure, use a different overload: os << TiffCraft::Type::BYTE; and os << TiffCraft::Tag::ImageWidth; and IFD/Entry? Keep simple and safe: use Tag and Type overloads plus IFD::Entry if easy. Minimal safe: Tag and Type. But better coverage: also TiffImage? default-constructible? Check quickly. Keep to Tag + Type to be safe — the point is link-level ODR, any operator<< works.
   Forward declaration for B: declare `std::string twoTuLinkTestA();` in B.
7. tests/twoTuLinkTestB.cpp — defines main(): calls twoTuLinkTestA(), prints nothing critical, also uses operator<< on TiffCraft::Tag itself, returns 0 on success (or 1 on empty string).

**D. tests/CMakeLists.txt** — after the existing tiffExporterTest block, add:
   ```cmake
   add_executable(twoTuLinkTest twoTuLinkTestA.cpp twoTuLinkTestB.cpp)
   target_link_libraries(twoTuLinkTest PRIVATE TiffCraft)
   add_test(NAME twoTuLinkTest COMMAND twoTuLinkTest)
   add_executable(readmeUsageTest readmeUsageTest.cpp)
   target_link_libraries(readmeUsageTest PRIVATE TiffCraft)
   add_test(NAME readmeUsageTest COMMAND readmeUsageTest ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/libtiff-pics/pc260001.tif)
   ```

**E. tests/readmeUsageTest.cpp** — the exact README.md "Usage" quick-start snippet, with a header comment "Keep in sync with README.md (the Usage quick-start). If this file and README diverge, update both.":
   ```cpp
   // license header block (copy tiffImageTest.cpp's style, brief)
   #include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>
   #include <functional>
   int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
     if (argc < 2) { return 1; }
     TiffCraft::TiffExporterAny tiffExporter;
     TiffCraft::load(argv[1], std::ref(tiffExporter));
     auto image = tiffExporter.takeImage();
     return image.data.empty() ? 1 : 0;   // nullptr check not needed; data empty check is fine
   }
   ```
   (Return non-zero on failure so ctest fails.) Match README snippet body exactly for the load/takeImage lines.

**F. CHANGELOG.md** — clarify the multi-IFD note under [0.2.0-Unreleased] Fixed: change "TiffExporterAny now resets its multi-IFD state per IFD, so images with multiple IFDs export correctly instead of silently skipping later IFDs." to also state the last-wins semantics explicitly, e.g.: "...per IFD; each IFD is exported and the last successfully exported image wins (previously later IFDs were silently skipped)." Keep one bullet, minimal edit.

### Verification you must run
- cmake --preset gcc-linux-release && cmake --build --preset gcc-linux-release -j && ctest --preset gcc-linux-release --output-on-failure — expect ALL tests pass (tiffImageTest, tiffExporterTest, twoTuLinkTest, readmeUsageTest). Report exact output.
- Do NOT commit. The orchestrator commits.
- Do not modify include/ headers (except reading). Do not modify README.md. Do not commit anything.

Report: files added/modified, exact ctest output, any deviations.

+TEST_CASE("Malformed TIFF input") {
+
+  { // (a) ASCII entry with count == 0
+    std::stringstream stream;
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(0x4949), false); // "II"
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(42), false);     // Magic number
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint32_t>(8), false);      // First IFD offset
+    // IFD at offset 8
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(1), false);                      // 1 entry
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(Tag::ImageDescription), false);  // Tag
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(Type::ASCII), false);            // Type
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint32_t>(0), false);                      // Count == 0
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint32_t>(0), false);                      // Inline value
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint32_t>(0), false);                      // Next IFD offset
+    CHECK_THROWS_AS(TiffImage::read(stream), std::runtime_error);
+  }
+
+  { // (b) Cyclic IFD offset
+    std::stringstream stream;
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(0x4949), false); // "II"
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(42), false);     // Magic number
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint32_t>(8), false);      // First IFD offset
+    // IFD at offset 8: 0 entries, next IFD offset points back to itself
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(0), false);      // 0 entries
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint32_t>(8), false);      // Next IFD offset (cyclic)
+    CHECK_THROWS_AS(TiffImage::read(stream), std::runtime_error);
+  }
+
+  { // (c) Truncated strip: strip data is missing from the stream
+    std::vector<TiffImage::IFD::Entry> entries;
+    auto addEntry = [&entries](
+      uint16_t tag, Type type, uint32_t count,
+      const std::vector<uint8_t>& values,
+      uint32_t valueOffset = 0, bool mustSwap = false) {
+        std::stringstream stream;
+        // Write the entry
+        write_IFD_entry(
+          stream, static_cast<Tag>(tag), type, count,
+          reinterpret_cast<const std::byte*>(values.data()),
+          valueOffset, mustSwap);
+        // Read the entry back
+        TiffImage::IFD::Entry entry = TiffImage::IFD::Entry::read(stream, mustSwap);
+        // Add the entry to the vector
+        entries.push_back(entry);
+    };
+    // Entries must be sorted in ascending tag order
+    addEntry(0x0103, Type::SHORT, 1, { 1 });                  // Compression = none
+    addEntry(0x0106, Type::SHORT, 1, { 0 });                  // PhotometricInterpretation = WhiteIsZero
+    addEntry(0x0111, Type::LONG, 1, { 100, 0, 0, 0 });        // StripOffsets = 100 (beyond end of stream)
+    addEntry(0x0117, Type::LONG, 1, { 232, 3, 0, 0 });        // StripByteCounts = 1000
+
+    std::stringstream stream;
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(0x4949), false); // "II"
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(42), false);     // Magic number
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint32_t>(8), false);      // First IFD offset
+    // IFD at offset 8 (only the IFD; the strip data is not written)
+    write_IFD(stream, entries, false);
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint32_t>(0), false);      // Next IFD offset
+    CHECK_THROWS_AS(
+      load(stream, [](auto&&...) { }, LoadParams{}),
+      std::runtime_error);
+  }
+
+  { // (d) RATIONAL entry with a zero denominator
+    std::stringstream stream;
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(0x4949), false); // "II"
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(42), false);     // Magic number
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint32_t>(8), false);      // First IFD offset
+    // IFD at offset 8
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(1), false);                 // 1 entry
+    writeValue(stream, static_cast<uint16_t>(Tag::XResolution), false);  // Tag
